summary: Egress address-mapping appliance rewrites IPv4 dest to IPv6-mapped (::ffff:) causing TLS SNI / certname mismatch on artifact CDN
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent failures downloading model/artifact shards from our CDN during Private deployment. Failures started after a third-party egress appliance firmware upgrade.
Impact: Artifact download errors for a subset of hosts in the customer's VPC causing model pull backoffs and degraded inference capacity during nightly batch pulls. Approx 20% of download attempts return TLS/hostname verification errors.
Environment: Private deployment (VPC + VPCE) in us-west-2, traffic egresses through customer-managed transit appliance (vendor: NetPathX, model NX-2100).
Observed behaviour: TLS handshake fails with certificate name mismatch reported by s3 client. Packet captures show destination IP in outbound TCP/TLS frames as IPv6-mapped address (::ffff:10.12.34.56) while SNI contains the original hostname (cdn.redwood-inference.com). The CDN serves a certificate for cdn.redwood-inference.com, but some client libs attempt host validation against the numeric destination IP when the socket peer address is an IPv6-mapped address, causing verification failure.
Expected behaviour: Egress appliance should preserve IPv4 destination addresses (10.12.34.56) in the IP layer when performing NAT/translation or preserve original socket peer for TLS validation, not convert to IPv6-mapped format.
Steps to reproduce: 1) From a serving node in the customer's private deploy, attempt a presigned shard range download via our SDK. 2) Observe intermittent TLS hostname verification failures in the agent logs. 3) Run tcpdump during failing request to inspect IP addressing and TLS ClientHello.
Relevant logs/snippets: see `logs` field for captures and errors.
steps_to_reproduce: Run tcpdump on node: tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/shard-fail.pcap host 10.12.34.56
Re-run download and observe TLS handshake failures in agent logs and PCAP shows ::ffff:10.12.34.56 as destination IP for some flows
logs: 2026-03-12T03:42:11Z agent[pid=2345] ERROR shard-fetch: tls: certificate is valid for cdn.redwood-inference.com, not 10.12.34.56

OpenSSL s_client output (failing flow): CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 C = US, O = Redwood CDN, CN = cdn.redwood-inference.com
verify error:num=62:hostname mismatch
tcpdump excerpt: 14:22:18.123456 IP6 fe80::2 > ::ffff:10.12.34.56: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
Agent debug: outbound-dest-address=::ffff:10.12.34.56, SNI=cdn.redwood-inference.com, socket.getpeername() returned ('::ffff:10.12.34.56', 443)

investigation_notes: Confirmed failure class is not SNI stripping or TLS inspection — SNI in ClientHello intact and certificate presented by CDN is correct for hostname.

Socket peer address reported by the agent is ::ffff:10.12.34.56 for failing flows; some languages/libraries (older Go versions, older OpenSSL stacks) validate against numeric peer name if peer is an IP literal rather than hostname, causing mismatch.
PCAP shows appliance rewrote packets on egress: source stays 198.51.100.23, destination was transformed from IPv4 10.12.34.56 to IPv6 ::ffff:10.12.34.56 before sending to upstream transit link.
Scanned customer appliance config; 'enable-ipv4-mapping' flag toggled by default in vendor config template delivered with 3.2.1. Customer confirmed they used default template during upgrade.
No changes required in Redwood runtime — the issue is due to in-path address mangling by customer appliance that triggers host verification edge-cases in client libraries.
hypothesis: Vendor firmware 3.2.1 introduced an aggressive translation mode that maps IPv4 destinations into IPv6-mapped (::ffff:) addresses for egress to support an ISP IPv6-only peering. The appliance incorrectly applies this mapping to flows that are still IPv4-capable towards the CDN, causing socket peername to appear as an IP literal to the local TLS stack.

Affected client stacks that perform hostname verification against the numeric peer address fail because they do not prefer SNI/hostname when peername is an IP literal. This is intermittent because not all upstream paths trigger the appliance translation (dependent on ISP route selection).
action_items: Advise customer to apply vendor hotfix 3.2.2 which disables IPv4->IPv6-mapped rewrite by default (vendor hotfix confirmed 2026-03-13)
Customer to roll hotfix to prod and monitor shard download success rate for 24h
Support to add detection rule in agent logs to surface 'peer returned as ::ffff:' and create alert when rate > 1%
Infra Eng to update Confluence runbook with vendor firmware caveat and mitigation steps
resolution_notes: 2026-03-14: Vendor hotfix 3.2.2 applied to transit appliance across customer VPC (per FinOak Network Ops).
Post-deploy validation: artifact download success rate restored to baseline (99.98%) after full rollout; no further hostname verification TLS errors observed in agent logs.
Workaround used during mitigation: temporarily route a subset of nodes to IGW (bypass appliance) to unblock critical model pulls.
Longer term: added agent-level telemetry to detect IPv6-mapped peer addresses and surface in Console per-route error summaries; documented vendor firmware caveat in runbook.
root_cause: Third-party egress appliance firmware (NetPathX NX 3.2.1) enabled IPv4->IPv6-mapped address rewrite for certain egress flows, causing socket peer to be an IP literal and triggering hostname verification failures in some TLS client stacks.
follow_up: SRE to ship an agent telemetry PR that emits a metric when peer address contains '::ffff:' (PR linked in related_github_prs)
Customer Success to verify none of the customer's edge devices still have default 'enable-ipv4-mapping' enabled after next maintenance window
Eng to add FAQ entry for IP-mapping-induced TLS verification failures in Private deploy support docs
